newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in dull trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little changed against the dollar in dull late trading on Thursday, with further pressure seen on swaps, dealers said.
"It's a stagnant market. There is nothing much going on," one Japanese bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,325.15/25.20 at 0850 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,325.50/26.50. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,324.0/24.5 and 2,324.0/24.4, respectively.
One U.S. bank dealer said sentiment on the rupiah remained strong despite ample rupiah supply.
Dealers said the central bank did not buy any dollars from the market after raising its fixing late on Thrusday.
They said the rate did not fall out of the band.
The central bank raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,325/2,517 and the conversion rate to 2,325/2,373.
The U.S. bank dealer said offshore operators seemed to maintain outright selling, keeping spot and swap rates under sustained pressure.
He said the dollar-rupiah rate was expected to range between 2,325.50 and 2,326.50 on Friday.
One local bank dealer said overnight money fell to 6.5 percent late in the afternoon on excess rupiah supply.
Overnight swap was at 0.15/0.20 and tom/next at 1.0/1.1.
One-month swap edged down to 16.75/17.5 from 17.0/17.5, two to 32.75/34.25 from 33.5/35.0, three to 49.00/49.75 from 49.50/50.75 and six to 97.0/98.0 from 98.0/99.5 points.
